question: Should OpenClaw reserve the top-level `auth` CLI namespace for core model-auth shortcuts even though installed plugins may already own that root command?
rationale: The repository currently exposes arbitrary plugin root commands, so choosing core ownership changes a user-visible extension contract rather than being a mechanical alias decision.

options.title: Keep auth plugin-extensible
options.body: Retain `openclaw models auth list` as the supported command and do not add the conflicting top-level core namespace.

options.title: Reserve auth for core
options.body: Approve core ownership only with documented collision or migration behavior, compatibility tests, and live upgrade proof covering an installed plugin-owned `auth` command.

recommendation.title: Keep auth plugin-extensible
recommendation.body: Retain `openclaw models auth list` as the supported command and do not add the conflicting top-level core namespace.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is their introduction of the plugin CLI registration system, and they are already connected to this PR’s discussion.
